messages.content:
Write ONE original fictional document, not JSON and not multiple versions.
Return only the complete document. It MUST contain 900 to 1100 words of substantive content.
Use eight connected paragraphs of roughly 95 words each and a numbered section with four
substantial items. Do not stop after an outline or summary. This length is required because
the small rewriter must learn to preserve information across a full long document.
Use the supplied fictional situation. Expand it with internally consistent concrete details,
uncertainty, conditions, and follow-up requests. Include all protected anchors exactly, with
the quoted line inside a direct quote. Keep quotes and code/path literals exact.
For /slack write a long casual team message. For /transcribe write a long, clean spoken account,
with natural conversational wording. For /prompt write a detailed REQUEST for a useful task,
including background and all constraints; do not perform the task. For /polish write clear plain
prose. Do not mention a formatter, dataset, word count, mode, or these authoring instructions.
Preserve the feature guidance. Include a numbered section, full paragraphs, a direct quote,
and a condition that refers to information elsewhere. Make the final paragraph substantive.

Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. result.text:
Jules, I’m going over the evening plans now, and I wanted to give you a clear spoken update before we settle the tables and send everyone the final details. You’re checking 95 score sheets, so I don’t want to assume that the totals, the player names, or the spare-piece count are already settled just because most of the paperwork is in one place. The attached note says, “Count the spare pieces.” I’m treating that sentence as information from the note, not as confirmation that anyone has counted them yet. That distinction matters for what we promise the group.

The plan as I understand it is to meet at the community room at six thirty, with the first game starting once people have found their seats and we have sorted out the boxes. We’re expecting a mix of regulars and a few newcomers, so it would help to keep one table open until we know how many people are actually coming. The schedule can stay flexible by about fifteen minutes, especially if the sheet check takes longer than expected. I’d rather have a calm start and accurate results than announce a precise seating chart that we then have to change.

For the score sheets, could you check that each page has a game title, a date, and legible player names before you compare the scores? If a sheet is missing one of those details, please flag it instead of guessing what was intended. Some of the games use different scoring systems, so a total that looks unusual may still be correct; the rules card or the players’ notes should be the reference. If two entries appear to conflict, mark both for review and tell me which pages they are on. That way we can resolve a specific discrepancy rather than recalculate everything without knowing where the problem began.

I also need a definite follow-up about the pieces, not just a general note that the games are ready. Please count the spare pieces for each box separately and write down the game name and the number you find. If the pieces are mixed together, keep them in a separate tray while you identify them, and don’t assign an uncertain piece to a box based only on its color. The count has not been confirmed, so we should say that plainly in the group update. Once you’ve checked it, send me the box-by-box results and tell me whether any game is missing something needed to play.

Here’s the order I suggest. Number one, finish the sheet review and note any unclear names, dates, or totals. Number two, check the spare pieces for each game and record the count separately. Number three, compare any doubtful score entry with the relevant rules or player note, and ask me before changing a result if the evidence still doesn’t settle it. Number four, send a short status message with what is ready, what is waiting, and what decision you need from me. If you reach the piece count before the sheet review is finished, you can report that count right away, but leave the overall evening plan marked provisional.

There’s a file called `board-games_2.txt` that may help with the schedule and the game list. Please compare it with the boxes on the table, because the file might describe the intended lineup rather than what is physically available tonight. If the file lists a game that we don’t have, or the box has a different title than the list, tell me which entry differs and don’t silently substitute another game. If the list and the boxes agree, you can use the file’s order when laying out the tables. If they don’t agree, pause on the seating plan and send me the discrepancy before you print or post anything.

For the message to the group, I’d keep the wording friendly and practical: doors open at six thirty, we’ll start as soon as the tables are ready, and people can bring a favorite game if they want, but we can’t promise it will be included in the lineup. Please don’t announce final scores or say that every box has all its pieces until your checks are complete. If you find a shortage, let me know whether it affects play or is only a spare, since that changes whether we should remove the game, borrow a replacement, or simply mention the missing extra. If you can’t tell which case applies, leave that question open and ask me before sending the final message.

Once you’ve finished, please send me the exact number of score sheets reviewed, the names of any sheets that need attention, and the separate piece count for each box. Also tell me whether the schedule in `board-games_2.txt` matches what is actually available, and include any mismatch rather than just saying the file is out of date. Only after the count is checked should we add the extra action of preparing a borrowing request for replacements; if the count is still uncertain, don’t contact anyone yet. I’ll use your update to decide whether we keep the full lineup, adjust the tables, or ask someone to bring a specific game.
